skill.name: project-scaffolding
skill.description: Guided project scaffolding for web, backend, mobile, desktop, extension, serverless, library, CLI, and monorepo starters. It helps choose frameworks, runtimes, databases, testing, linting, Docker, and CI settings before generating starter files.
skill.summary: Create configured starter projects through a guided framework and tooling wizard.
skill.author: hmohamed01

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, generated template strings, and environment placeholders. No prompt-injection text, credential exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found. Confirmed risks are unvalidated scaffold output paths, unpinned native CLI guidance, and unsafe defaults in generated project templates.

remediation.issue: Project names are used as output paths without containment checks.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute paths, parent traversal, and path separators, then resolve the destination and verify it stays inside an allowed base directory.

remediation.issue: Native CLI guidance uses unpinned latest package generators.
remediation.suggestion: Pin generator versions, document required network access, and require explicit user confirmation before running external commands.

remediation.issue: Generated templates include default database credentials and known secret-key fallbacks.
remediation.suggestion: Generate random local-only secrets, require production secrets through environment variables, and mark sample database credentials as development-only.

remediation.issue: Generated Flask settings default to debug mode.
remediation.suggestion: Default DEBUG to false and make development debug mode an explicit option in generated projects.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Project Path Can Escape Workspace
semantic_findings.description: The CLI passes the raw project name into ProjectConfig, joins it with the base path, and then writes generated files. A name with path separators or parent traversal can place output outside the intended project folder.

content.value_statement: Starting a new codebase requires many framework, testing, database, and deployment choices. This skill guides those choices and generates starter files for common project types.
actual_capabilities: Guides project type, language, package manager, database, testing, and DevOps choices.
Generates starters for frontend, backend, mobile, desktop, extension, serverless, library, CLI, and monorepo projects.
Creates framework files for React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Express, FastAPI, Django, Flask, and related stacks.
Adds common configuration for TypeScript, linting, formatting, tests, Docker, CI, and environment examples.
Provides reference guidance for framework options, architecture patterns, and project best practices.
limitations: Generated projects still need human review before production use.
Native CLI workflows may require installed tools, network access, and user confirmation.
The scaffold script does not install dependencies by itself.
Advanced framework versions and deployment targets may need manual updates.

use_cases.title: Create a Frontend Starter
use_cases.description: Generate a React, Vue, Svelte, or Next.js project with TypeScript, styling, tests, and basic documentation.

use_cases.title: Start a Backend API
use_cases.description: Create a FastAPI, Django, Flask, Express, or NestJS service with database, testing, and container options.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Multi-Package Workspace
use_cases.description: Scaffold a monorepo with shared packages, app folders, workspace configuration, linting, and CI structure.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new static website named portfolio with responsive CSS, three pages, and a README.

prompt_templates.title: React Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React project named dashboard with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vitest, ESLint, and Prettier.

prompt_templates.title: Python API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI project named inventory-api with SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL settings, pytest, Docker, and GitHub Actions.

prompt_templates.title: Monorepo Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Turborepo workspace with a Next.js app, Node API package, shared UI package, Docker files, and CI checks.

output_examples.input: Create a React TypeScript dashboard with Tailwind and tests.
output: A new dashboard folder is created with Vite, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind configuration.
The project includes starter source files, test setup, linting, formatting, README, and environment example files.

output_examples.input: Create a FastAPI service with PostgreSQL and Docker.
output: A backend service folder is created with application modules, settings, database session files, and test dependencies.
The project includes Docker assets, database configuration examples, dependency files, and startup notes.

output_examples.input: Create a TypeScript library package with tests.
output: A package folder is created with source files, test files, TypeScript settings, build tooling, and README guidance.
The starter is ready for dependency installation, local testing, and further package customization.

best_practices: Review generated secrets, database settings, and debug flags before deployment.
Run dependency installation and tests in a controlled workspace after scaffolding.
Pin framework and CLI versions when reproducibility or supply-chain control matters.
anti_patterns: Do not use generated development credentials in staging or production.
Do not run native CLI generators from untrusted networks without approval.
Do not scaffold into paths that include parent traversal or sensitive directories.

faq.question: What project types can this skill create?
faq.answer: It covers common frontend, backend, mobile, desktop, extension, serverless, library, CLI, and monorepo starters.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: The included scaffold script writes project files. Native CLI workflows may require separate command execution.

faq.question: Can I choose databases and tooling?
faq.answer: Yes. The wizard covers databases, ORMs, tests, linting, formatting, Docker, CI, and related options.

faq.question: Is the generated code production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starter baseline. Review security settings, dependencies, secrets, and deployment configuration first.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Turborepo, Nx Workspace, and pnpm Workspace structures.
